matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction) and determine the numeric imbalance; then look for a single‑stick move that can adjust the values by exactly that amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which side to increase or decrease.
matchstick.example: Changing a numeral by moving a stick without checking the numeric difference, resulting in a new equation that is still false.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If a side needs to increase by exactly 5 and a V appears there, move a diagonal stick to the V to turn it into an X, raising its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric shortfall is 5 and a V is present on the side that must increase.
matchstick.example: Adding a diagonal stick to a V but not forming a proper X, leaving the numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already contains at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I, thereby increasing the target by 1 and decreasing the source by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 2 and both sides contain numerals with at least one I.
matchstick.example: Removing an I from a numeral that only contains a single I, making the source numeral disappear.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) appear, you can relocate one horizontal stick from the equals to the minus, turning the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false and swapping the operators could balance the numeric values.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=', leaving only one horizontal, so the equality sign becomes a minus sign unintentionally.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If a side needs to decrease by exactly 5 and an X appears there, move one diagonal stick from the X to reposition it as a V, lowering its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric excess is 5 and an X is present on the side that must decrease.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and not repositioning it, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, you can move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side that is too large to a numeral on the side that is too small, adjusting both sides by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 2 and both sides contain at least one I.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a side that is already correct, making the imbalance larger instead of reducing it.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains the pattern 'XI', moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes the numeral to 'IX', decreasing its value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a numeral by 2 and it contains the sequence 'XI'.
matchstick.example: Moving the I but leaving the X unchanged, resulting in an invalid numeral like 'I X' with extra spacing.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a plus sign is present, moving its vertical stick to a numeral adds an I (increase by 1) and simultaneously changes the plus into a minus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 1 and a plus sign is available.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick but forgetting to adjust the operator, leaving a malformed '+' sign.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick from the equality sign, ensure that the remaining symbol still forms a valid '=' (i.e., retains two horizontals) or a valid '-' (if you intend to change it).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Taking one horizontal from '=', leaving only a single horizontal, which no longer represents a valid equality sign.

matchstick.title: Reposition I relative to V to change IV to VI (or VI to IV)
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical I‑stick from before a V to after the V (or vice‑versa) changes the numeral from subtractive notation (IV) to additive notation (VI) or the reverse, adjusting its value by ±2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 2 and the side that must change contains the numeral IV (or VI).
matchstick.example: Moving the I from before V but not repositioning it after V, producing an invalid numeral such as 'IIV'.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring the structural constraints of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before removing a stick, verify that the source numeral will still be a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move and neglects the requirement to output a complete, syntactically correct equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always ensure the final answer is a single line of the form "<equation>" containing a valid left side, '=', and a valid right side.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the two horizontal bars of '=' as independent, forgetting that both are needed for a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If a stick is taken from '=', make sure the remaining symbol still has two horizontals (or intentionally change it to a minus and adjust the other operator accordingly).

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after forming a visually plausible equation without checking the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, recompute the numeric values of both sides and confirm they are equal before outputting the answer.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes performs a multi‑step transformation in a single reasoning step, effectively moving several sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict the transformation to a single stick relocation; any additional changes must be avoided.
